document.title: Afghanistan: Pakistanis to Regulate Wheat and Fuel Trade to Gain Leverage Over Taliban (Islama 06882)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Confidential] Pakistan tightens regulation of wheat and fuel trade with Afghanistan, partly to gain leverage over the Taliban and to curb drug trafficking, demanding hard currency instead of drug 'powder'. Officials say they deal only with the Taliban, and Pakistan continues to back a Taliban takeover.

mentions.quote: IN A JULY 26 SPEECH AT TORKHAM ON THE AFGHAN BORDER WITH THE NORTHWEST FRONTIER PROVINCE, NAWAZ PROMISED THAT TRADE WITH AFGHANISTAN WOULD BE REGULATED
THE PROCESS OF CREATING LEVERAGE TO USE ON THE TALIBAN HAD BEEN ENERGIZED BY A DECISION OF THE PRIME MINISTER IN JUNE THAT THE BORDER HAD TO REGULATED
COMMERCE MINISTER MOHAMMAD DAR MADE SIMILAR REMARKS ON AUGUST 9.
THAT SAME DAY HE HAS PUSHED FOREIGN MINISTER GOHAR AYUB KHAN TO GET IT DONE.
USE IT, ONCE IN PLACE, TO MODERATE THE TALIBAN. SIMONS
THE AMBASSADOR, ACCOMPANIED BY AC-COUNSELOR, RAISED THE ISSUE OF THE CROSS BORDER TRADE IN WHEAT.

events.description: April wheat crisis prompted GOP internal discussion of regulating trade with Afghanistan.
Pakistan's precipitate recognition of the Taliban in late May.
Prime Minister decided the Afghan border had to be regulated.
Nawaz Sharif speech at Torkham promising regulated trade with Afghanistan.
Commerce Minister Mohammad Dar made similar remarks about regulating trade.
GOP officials told the US Ambassador an agreement with the Taliban on wheat sales (600,000 tons at 9,500 rupees/ton, cash in US dollars) was reached though not finalized; POL to follow.
April wheat crisis prompts internal GOP discussion of regulating trade with Afghanistan.
Pakistan recognizes the Taliban government in late May.
Prime Minister decides the border must be regulated.
Nawaz Sharif speaks at Torkham, promising Afghan trade will be regulated under an established policy.
A GOP official gives the Embassy POLCOUNS details on the leverage policy.
Commerce Minister Mohammad Dar makes remarks on regulating Afghan trade.
The Ambassador raises trade regulation with a GOP official, who confirms the leverage aim.
Ambassador meets GOP officials; told of an agreement to sell 600,000 tons of wheat to the Taliban, to be formalized via Gohar Ayub Khan.
GOP agrees in writing to sell 600,000 tons of wheat at 9,500 PK Rs/ton in dollars to the Taliban, split between Torkham and Chaman.
Pakistan's government recognized the Taliban government in late May.
Wheat trade regulation system nearly agreed, with Afghans issuing permits that Pakistan would honor for purchases in Peshawar and Quetta; POL system to follow shortly.
U.S. Embassy Islamabad cable 06882 sent to State Department assessing Pakistan's attempt to gain leverage over the Taliban via trade regulation.

key_claims: The Government of Pakistan is moving to regulate wheat and fuel trade with Afghanistan, with the objective appearing primarily political: gaining leverage over the Taliban.
The GOP agreed in writing to sell 600,000 tons of wheat to the Taliban for US dollars, split between Torkham and Chaman, at a fixed price of 9,500 rupees per ton.
A GOP official publicly denied a political aim, citing economic and narcotics concerns, such as ensuring payment in hard currency rather than drugs.
Privileged access to Pakistani food and fuel has been the Taliban's major input to its war effort in recent years.
The GOP may be motivated by concern that it has become too closely associated with the Taliban after its recognition in late May 1997.
The US Embassy views Pakistani efforts as positive if the GOP uses leverage to moderate the Taliban.
